steps.what: Identify patient records and verify source documents and encounter links
Compile document copies and record links into the patient record assembly
Review record completeness and accept the compiled patient record version

tasks.design: Test native document assembly in {OTHER}, the clinical record system, using a checked manifest of existing documents in {DOCS}. Stage the exact documents without rewriting clinical meaning, then have the specialist review completeness and accept the record version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate document stores can require repeated copying and linking.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document interfaces can assemble identified existing records with provenance.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong-patient links, missing documents and conflicting clinical content need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an incomplete or inconsistent dossier and obtaining clarification.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated assembly while retaining record-quality decisions.

reach.learn: Encounter linkage and document version control

evidence.claim: A provenance-preserving document assembly interface is a plausible design; the supplied clinical scribe cases do not establish its local labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is assembly and maintenance of existing signed records, not clinician authorship, coding, research extraction or permission to release records. Those remain separate.

Clinicians produce signed documents during existing care, with document ID/version, patient ID, encounter ID, author, date and signature status before s1. Specialist in s1 verifies identities and captures the exact document manifest and intended record location; capture and manual resolution retain 30 baseline hours.

Integration consumes only the checked manifest and original documents. Missing identifiers, ambiguous links or unavailable interfaces return to manual assembly; no free clinical summary or completeness flag is assumed.
Native configuration is tested first; existing automatic filing earns no saving. Additional access and mapping support is counted below.
research_questions: Is repeated manual assembly substantial after identity checks, exception work and interface upkeep?

already_counted.description: Identity capture, completeness review and acceptance

incremental.description: Maintain mapping tests and exception rules

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient and encounter IDs, document IDs and versions, links and record destination; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+0+35=65, gross=35, focal upkeep=8, net=27. Range 0-10 assumes repeated manual linking across stores; existing automatic filing or unreliable identifiers remove the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Identify the coding episode and gather complete patient documentation and classification guidance
Abstract patient findings and propose standard classification codes

loop.purpose: Suggest source-supported codes within the selected classification
loop.input: Checked episode packet and exact classification edition
loop.output: Candidate codes with source spans, sequencing rationale and unresolved ambiguities
loop.check: Specialist checks documented diagnosis, negation, timing, code specificity, exclusions and sequencing against original records and coding guidance
loop.stop: One proposal and correction; ambiguous documentation returns to clinician query and manual coding
loop.why_not_simpler: Clinical narrative needs contextual abstraction before fixed code validation

steps.what: Resolve coding uncertainties and accept the final abstraction and codes

tasks.design: Configure the native coding assistant in {OTHER}, a clinical coding system, before custom orchestration. The specialist verifies proposed abstractions against original text, resolves queries and accepts the exact code version; grouping and submission remain separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative abstraction and code lookup require repeated source comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-grounded coding suggestions exist, but require local evaluation and human checking.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible code can misrepresent uncertain diagnoses or episode sequencing.
tasks.human_edge: Applying coding guidance to documented clinical context and recognising when clarification is necessary.
tasks.altitude: More attention to ambiguous coding cases without removing final code accountability.

reach.task: Review coding provenance in a data extract

evidence.claim: Dutch Hospital Data supports ICD-10 coding of day admissions from clinical text; its provider figures do not establish accuracy or time savings for all coding settings.
The proposed review time and savings are local E1 scenarios, not transferred provider results.

assumptions: Boundary includes coding episode preparation, abstraction and acceptance only. Assembly of the longitudinal dossier and downstream grouping are excluded; any shared episode preparation must be assigned once in roll-up.

Clinicians supply signed source documentation before s1. Specialist in s1 verifies patient/episode IDs, document versions, episode dates, classification edition and scope, capturing the packet manifest. Missing documentation is obtained manually; no free complete clinical facts table is assumed.
Queries generated during review are answered by clinicians in the existing clarification process; no reduction in their time is claimed. Extra clarification burden is allowed below.
Native coding support and fixed code validation are tested first; no automatic coding acceptance by confidence score alone is proposed.
research_questions: Does blinded coding comparison show time reduction after meaning checks, corrections and clinician queries?

already_counted.description: Packet capture, code meaning verification and final coding acceptance

incremental.description: Maintain coding examples and review error patterns
Interface support and additional clinical clarification

approvals.approved_version: Exact episode, source versions, classification edition, code set and sequencing; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+40*0.60+25=84, gross=16, focal upkeep=8, net=8. Range 0-3 assumes documented routine episodes; ambiguity or existing assistants may remove the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify grouping inputs and run the appropriate diagnosis-related group software
Resolve grouping exceptions and accept the patient group assignment

tasks.design: Retain native grouping in {OTHER}, the clinical grouping system, and keep input verification and exception handling human. The statement already includes computer software, so its calculation runtime creates no new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Grouping depends on correct episode inputs and the applicable payment classification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing grouping software already applies deterministic grouping rules.
tasks.still_hard: Incorrect clinical coding or administrative context can produce a technically valid but inappropriate group.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising exceptions and directing corrections to the responsible source owner.

reach.learn: Local grouping rules and source ownership

evidence.claim: The task already uses grouping software; retaining verification and exception work earns no new saving from existing deterministic runtime.

assumptions: This branch applies where diagnosis-related grouping is actually used; national payment classifications differ and require local confirmation. Billing submission is outside the boundary.

Coding staff produce accepted episode codes in a separate coding task; registration staff produce episode IDs, dates and other grouper-required administrative fields during ordinary registration. In s1 specialist checks exact rule version and its required fields, resolves missing values manually and runs the existing tool; that effort is fully counted.
Upstream coding labour is excluded here and must be owned once in roll-up. No automatic transfer interface or free clinical correctness flag is proposed.
Native grouping is already the first option. No new implementation or capture requirement means zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Is there a separately observed manual transfer burden beyond existing native grouping?

already_counted.description: Input checking, software operation and grouping exception acceptance

incremental.description: No new upkeep beyond existing grouping work

approvals.approved_version: Exact episode inputs, code version, grouping rule version and resulting group; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100, gross=0, incremental=0, net=0. Existing grouping runtime is not human effort and no upstream coding saving is counted again.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify form purpose, permitted disclosure and source fields
Populate business or government forms with checked fields
Review prepared forms against instructions and assemble the submission proposal

tasks.design: Configure native form filling in {DOCS} from a checked field packet drawn from {OTHER}, the clinical record system. The specialist reviews instructions and permitted disclosure before providing a proposal to the authorised signatory; no automatic external submission is included.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated copying into fixed forms can create avoidable clerical work.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates can merge explicit fields without language generation.
tasks.still_hard: Form purpose and disclosure scope need checking for each request.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a request that exceeds authority or asks for unsupported information.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated transcription; request and disclosure judgement remain human.

reach.task: Clarify what a form request actually needs
reach.learn: Request scope and record disclosure boundaries

evidence.claim: Fixed form templates can populate checked fields; local labour saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Boundary ends at a checked proposal; signatory review, signatures and external submission retain their own existing time.

Specialist in s1 records form type/version, request ID, recipient, purpose, applicable disclosure authority, required field names, exact values and source references. Field capture and any extraction are included in s1; missing or narrative-only values are handled manually rather than inferred.
Existing record owners supply source facts in ordinary work; no new data feed or free permission flag is assumed. Permission is interpreted by the specialist before templating.
Test native merge fields first; no saving where the form is already populated automatically.
unknowns: Recurring form types and current automation
research_questions: Do repeated fixed forms save enough transcription time after capture, checking and template upkeep?

already_counted.description: Field capture, disclosure judgement and final form checking

incremental.description: Maintain form versions and mapping tests
Record access and form integration support

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+0+25=55, gross=45, focal upkeep=9, net=36. Range 0-12 assumes recurrent fixed forms and reliable records; bespoke narrative requests or existing autofill remove the gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Focuses on provenance, coding meaning and record exceptions while reducing repeated copying where it exists.
reach: Discuss source lineage with health information technologists and request scope with patient representatives
role.ambitious_version: A records specialist who improves traceability without confusing automated assembly with clinical correctness.
